verses.mystical_translation: The old light set—another lamp steps to the stand; the household's long glow takes a new, troubled flame.
Many names arrayed around the one who takes the throne—echoes of family that will not be spared.
Silver and towns as hedge and favor—birthright chooses the throne though gifts scatter to many.
A crown knit by blood; fraternal names fall into silence beneath the blade of stability.
A reign measured in years: the calendar records a brief orbit that will end in ruin.
Alliance by marriage guides the path; similarity to Ahab's house shapes the moral judgment.
Covenant restrains the sweep of judgment; a lamp's promise endures though the flame be dimmed.
Border peoples take advantage: the household loses its sway where it once held rule.
A nocturnal strike; the king strikes the circle that threatens him but the revolt will not be fully undone.
One loss leads to another—cities that once acknowledged the house depart when trust in YHWH is forsaken.
High places rise and the city is drawn into cultic prostitution—compulsion replaces covenantal worship.
A prophetic sword written: the voice of the northern prophet invokes the Davidic God to judge royal deviation.
The accusation pairs cult and kin-slaying: moral corruption and bloodshed named together as treason against heart and household.
Judgment touches the intimate and the material alike; the household and property are set as signs.
A slow corporeal unraveling; the body becomes the text of punishment, day by day.
Neighboring warrior-spi­rits are roused as instruments of disruption—external forces answer an inner turning away.
Loot and lineage are taken together: the house is emptied of its wealth and its heirs, save one small ember.
The covenantal judge turns the wound inward; an incurable disease marks the body's indictment.
A slow dissolving ends in death; even the funerary rites are diminished—honor is withheld as part of the story.
A short, disfavored stint—buried in the city of David but excluded from royal sepulchres, his memory marked by absence of honor.

contemplative_note: Power concentrated by violence yields isolation and bodily ruin; covenantal promise restrains total destruction even as judgment proceeds.
safety_note: Contains descriptions of familial slaughter, forced cultic sexual acts, and violent conquest; these are preserved for accuracy, not endorsement.
